answer: Tide-Locked Agent Registry. Each epoch, a registration window opens at a time derived from a verifiable random beacon (e.g., a delay-encrypted seed). An agent must submit its identity proof within that window; the beacon also selects which karst-like sparse slot in a fixed capacity table it may occupy. Miss the window and you wait for the next unpredictable epoch. An attacker cannot precompute slot availability or window timing, so bulk pre-registration fails — each identity must be live and responsive at a random moment. The marble-like fixed slot count caps registrations per epoch.
